summary: Jaro’s historic public square brings together a bandstand, monuments and the free-standing Jaro Belfry. It is a place to understand the district’s civic life, distinct from the cathedral across the road.
overview: Jaro Plaza, also called Graciano Lopez Jaena Park, is a public square in the Jaro district of Iloilo City. The bandstand and monuments give the square a civic character, while the free-standing belfry is a prominent landmark within its setting. The plaza is named for the Ilonggo journalist and reformist Graciano Lopez Jaena, whose monument is one of its recognizable features.

The square belongs to the heritage landscape of Jaro rather than being an extension of its cathedral. Jaro Cathedral, the former municipal hall and other historic buildings help explain the surrounding district, but each is a separate place. A visit can focus on the plaza’s monuments and bandstand, then continue to those neighboring landmarks when access allows. Restoration has changed parts of the plaza over time; an older photograph or video is useful for orientation, not proof of today’s layout.
